decisions.reason: The cited restriction-filtration proof explicitly constructs U from states with site n a defect (steps 1.1–2.1), and identifies the quotient by cutting the arc ending at n (steps 2.2–3.1). Its statement is abstract, but these proved maps are available. Gram steps 3.1–5.1 then establish the loop-count blocks and Schur complement locally; they do not infer them from an unspecified exact sequence.

The Statement asserts precisely semisimplicity and trace degeneracy at n=ell−1, and the proof establishes both. The title comparison is also supported by the existing direct dependency thm-temperley-lieb-complex-semisimplicity-classification, Statement clause 3 and proof step 1.4: semisimplicity holds exactly for n<ell, so failure at the next rank n=ell is already proved locally. Repeating that supplier conclusion is unnecessary. The contract and page promise the same boundary assertion.

reviews.reason: Checked all proof steps: lower-rank nondegeneracy gives an invariant orthogonal complement; simplicity and Schur give its scalar form. The four basis types give 0, B, and delta B blocks, yielding alpha=delta−1/previous alpha, with the empty A block at n=2p+1 and alpha=delta at n=2p. Pascal exponents solve both determinant recurrences, including p=1,2; polynomial continuation concerns the entire product. No choice axiom or unsupported splitting is used. The item, statement, contract and page require no repair.

Order ell>=3 excludes q=±1 and delta=0, gives [1],…,[ell−1] nonzero and [ell]=0. The recursion-properties supplier therefore gives a nonzero idempotent p with one-dimensional corner and zero trace. Cyclicity gives tau(px)=tau(pxp); the corner then makes this zero for every x. Thus p is a nonzero trace-radical vector. The separate classification proves semisimplicity at ell−1 and nonsemisimplicity at ell. Primitivity follows from the one-dimensional corner. No item, contract or page change is needed.
